mainTopic: Weighing meat and sharpening knives on יום טוב: what looks like weekday work, and the הלכה about מכשירי אוכל נפש
overview: The משנה records a מחלוקת about weighing meat on יום טוב. רבי יהודה allows weighing it against a vessel or a cleaver, while חכמים forbid using a scale at all, not even to keep meat safe from mice. The גמרא adds related rules: an expert butcher may not weigh meat by hand or in water, a handle may not be cut into meat with a tool but may be made by hand, and meat may be marked to show whose it is. When two sages weighed portion against portion, the גמרא explains they followed רבי יהושע. רב יוסף rules like him based on a משנה in בכורות, and אביי rejects that proof in two ways. A second משנה forbids sharpening a knife on יום טוב but allows rubbing one knife against another. The גמרא gives several versions of שמואל's comment about sharpening versus removing fat. It then shows the ban does not follow רבי יהודה, who permits מכשירי אוכל נפש, and רב חסדא agrees the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. A story about רבא begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: weighing meat against a vessel or cleaver
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה allows weighing meat on יום טוב against a vessel or a cleaver, not against real weights.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יהודה says: A person may weigh meat against a vessel or against a cleaver.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with רבי יהודה's view. A person may weigh meat on יום טוב against an object like a vessel or a cleaver, instead of against normal weights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weighing with real weights looks like a weekday business act. Balancing the meat against a pot or a knife is a different, unusual way to do it. Later the seller can weigh that pot or knife and work out how heavy the meat was.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the opening text being discussed)

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A person may weigh meat
against a vessel
or against a cleaver.
phrases.notes: He sets the meat on one side of the scale and the pot or cleaver on the other, then weighs that object after יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שׁוֹקֵל אָדָם בָּשָׂר כְּנֶגֶד הַכְּלִי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, on יום טוב one may weigh meat against a vessel or cleaver, but not against standard weights.

steps.title: חכמים: no use of a scale at all
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree and forbid any use of a scale on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: One may not look at the pans of a scale at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue with רבי יהודה. They say a scale may not be used on יום טוב in any way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, even the vessel-or-cleaver trick is still weighing on a scale, so it is forbidden. The words 'at all' are unclear, and the גמרא will explain them next.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not pay attention to / look at
The pan of a balance scale

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
One may not look at the pans of a scale
at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם כׇּל עִיקָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposing view to רבי יהודה in the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, a scale may not be used at all on יום טוב.

steps.title: What does 'at all' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra words 'at all' in the חכמים's statement come to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is meant by 'at all'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'at all' means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'one may not use a scale' would already forbid the vessel trick. So the extra words 'at all' must include something more. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is meant by 'at all'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to explain a phrase in the חכמים's statement
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra case the words 'at all' come to forbid

steps.title: Even to protect meat from mice
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that you may not even put meat on a scale just to keep it away from mice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Even to guard it from mice.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. 'At all' means a person may not even use the scale as a safe place to keep meat from mice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the person has no plan to weigh anything. Still, meat sitting on a scale looks like weighing, so the חכמים forbid it. This is the extra case that 'at all' adds.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Even to protect it from mice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'At all' forbids even putting meat on a scale only to protect it from mice.

steps.title: Only when the scale hangs ready for weighing
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין limits שמואל's rule to a scale hanging by its weighing ring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said: And this is only when it hangs by its ring.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי בר אבין adds a limit to שמואל's rule. The ban applies only when the scale is hanging by its ring, ready to weigh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the scale is set up for weighing, meat on it looks like weighing. If it is hanging some other way and can't be used to weigh, it is just a container. Then you may use it to protect the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: The ring by which a scale hangs for weighing

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said:
And this applies only where it hangs by the ring.
phrases.notes: The ring is what lets the scale balance and weigh. Hung any other way, it's just a basket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case of step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Putting meat on a scale to protect it is forbidden only if the scale hangs in weighing position.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, a scale may not be used at all, not even to protect meat from mice. But this is only when the scale is hanging ready to weigh.

steps.title: An expert butcher may not weigh meat by hand
steps.stepSummary: שמואל forbids an expert butcher from judging meat's weight by hand on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: An expert butcher may not weigh meat by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another rule from שמואל. An expert butcher may not weigh meat on יום טוב by lifting it in his hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An expert can tell the exact weight just by holding the meat. For him, this works like a scale, so it is forbidden. The rule speaks only about an expert, whose hand-guess is truly exact.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
An expert butcher is forbidden to weigh
meat by hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַבָּח אוּמָּן אָסוּר לִשְׁקוֹל בָּשָׂר בַּיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related rule about other ways of weighing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב, an expert butcher may not judge meat's weight by hand.

steps.title: An expert butcher may not weigh meat with water
steps.stepSummary: שמואל also forbids an expert butcher from weighing meat by putting it in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: An expert butcher may not weigh meat in water.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, parallel rule from שמואל. An expert butcher may not weigh meat on יום טוב by putting it in water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Butchers could find the exact weight by putting meat in a marked tub and seeing how high the water rose. Since this gives an exact weight, it counts like weighing and is forbidden.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
An expert butcher is forbidden to weigh
meat in water.
phrases.notes: He reads the weight from how far the water rises against marks on the tub.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַבָּח אוּמָּן אָסוּר לִשְׁקוֹל בָּשָׂר בְּמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 6, a second way of weighing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב, an expert butcher may not weigh meat by putting it in water.

steps.title: No cutting a handle into meat
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי forbids making a carrying-handle hole in meat on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חייא בר אשי said: It is forbidden to make a handle in meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אשי gives a new rule. On יום טוב you may not cut a hole in meat to make a handle for carrying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting a handle into meat is something butchers do on regular weekdays. So it is forbidden on יום טוב. The next step will add a limit to this rule.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said:
It is forbidden to make a handle in meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another weekday-type act with meat that is forbidden on יום טוב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב, one may not cut a handle into meat.

steps.title: Making the handle by hand is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבינא allows making the handle by hand instead of with a tool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: But by hand it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא limits רב חייא בר אשי's rule. If the handle is made by hand, without a knife, it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is on the normal weekday way, which uses a tool. Poking a hole by hand is an unusual way to do it, so it does not look like weekday work.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
But by hand it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule of step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making a handle in meat by hand, without a tool, is permitted on יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב, acts that look like weekday weighing or butchering are forbidden. The חכמים of the משנה forbid using a scale. שמואל forbids an expert butcher from weighing by hand or with water. רב חייא בר אשי forbids cutting a handle with a tool. An unusual way, like making the handle by hand, is allowed (רבינא).

steps.title: Making a mark on meat is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא allows putting an identifying mark on meat on יום טוב, like רבה בר רב הונא, who cut his meat into triangles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is allowed to make a mark on meat on יום טוב. This is like what רבה בר רב הונא did: he cut his meat into triangle shapes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds one more rule about handling meat on יום טוב: you may mark it so people know whose it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 8-9 dealt with making a handle hole in meat. Here רב הונא allows a simple mark on the meat itself, and he gives a real-life example: רבה בר רב הונא cut his meat into triangles.

keyTerms.meaning: Three corners, meaning a triangle shape

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is permitted to make a sign on meat,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: like that of Rabba bar Rav Huna,
who would cut it into three-cornered pieces (triangles).
phrases.notes: The triangle shape showed that the meat was his, so it would not get mixed up with someone else's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מוּתָּר לַעֲשׂוֹת סִימָן בַּבָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the run of rules about preparing meat on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may make an identifying mark on meat on יום טוב.

steps.title: Two sages weighed portion against portion on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי weighed one portion of meat against another on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון the son of רבי would weigh one portion against another portion on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us what two great sages actually did. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They were not weighing meat against a measured weight. They put one portion on each side of the scale, so the two people sharing would get equal amounts. This practice now needs to be matched to a view in the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi,

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹקְלִין מָנָה כְּנֶגֶד מָנָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: would weigh one portion against another portion on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי שׁוֹקְלִין מָנָה כְּנֶגֶד מָנָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main topic of the משנה, weighing meat on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, these sages weighed portion against portion on יום טוב.

steps.title: Whose view did they follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view this practice follows, since neither רבי יהודה nor the רבנן seem to allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is not like רבי יהודה and not like the רבנן! If it is like רבי יהודה, he said a person may weigh meat against a vessel or a cleaver. Against a vessel, yes; against anything else, no! If it is like the רבנן, they said you may not look at the scale pans at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the sages' practice: it does not seem to fit either side of the מחלוקת in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה only allows weighing meat against a vessel or a cleaver, not against another portion of meat. The רבנן forbid using the scale at all. So weighing meat against meat seems to break both views.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose view is this?
A cleaver, a butcher's chopping knife
One does not look at or pay attention to

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה's view sounds lenient, but it is limited. He only allows a vessel or a cleaver as the counterweight, not another piece of meat.

phrases.english: In accordance with whose opinion?
Neither like Rabbi Yehuda nor like the Rabbis!
If like Rabbi Yehuda, didn't he say:
A person may weigh meat against a vessel
or against a cleaver.
Against a vessel, yes,
against anything else, no!
If like the Rabbis, didn't they say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם כׇּל עִיקָּר!
phrases.english: One may not look at the pans of a scale at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? לָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלֹא כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה allows only a vessel or cleaver as a counterweight, and the רבנן forbid the scale entirely, so weighing meat against meat fits neither view.

steps.title: They followed רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The sages followed רבי יהושע, who allows weighing portion against portion on יום טוב, as taught in a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They acted like רבי יהושע. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהושע says, one may weigh one portion against another portion on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: there is a third view, רבי יהושע's, and the sages followed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not record every opinion. A ברייתא brings רבי יהושע, who allows exactly what the sages did. So their practice has a clear source.

phrases.english: They acted in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua.
As it is taught in a baraita, Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹקְלִין מָנָה כְּנֶגֶד מָנָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: One may weigh portion against portion on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a third opinion not found in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only choices were רבי יהודה or the רבנן, and neither allows it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sages followed רבי יהושע, who allows weighing portion against portion.

steps.title: רב יוסף rules like רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע, because a משנה in בכורות agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע, since we learned a משנה in בכורות that agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף goes beyond explaining the sages' practice and makes it the actual הלכה. He also tells us he has a source, which the next step will quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 only showed the sages had someone to rely on. רב יוסף now says this is the binding ruling, because an unnamed משנה elsewhere matches רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law follows this opinion
Like him, in agreement with him

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua,
since we learned a mishna in Bekhorot in accordance with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 13 into a final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is that one may weigh portion against portion on יום טוב, like רבי יהושע.

steps.title: The proof from the משנה in בכורות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in בכורות allows weighing portion against portion with a בכור, matching רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: With disqualified קדשים, the profit from them goes to הקדש. And one may weigh portion against portion with a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that רב יוסף mentioned, to support his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat of a blemished בכור may not be sold by weight the normal way. Still, the משנה allows weighing one portion against another. That matches רבי יהושע: weighing portion against portion is treated differently from ordinary weighing.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial animals that became unfit, usually because of a blemish
The profit from them goes to the Temple treasury

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף rules that weighing one portion against another is allowed on יום טוב, like רבי יהושע. His support is that even with a בכור, where normal weighing is not allowed, this kind of weighing is permitted. אביי challenges this proof in the next two steps.

phrases.english: As we learned: Disqualified consecrated animals,
the benefit from them goes to the Temple treasury,
and one may weigh portion against portion with a firstborn.
phrases.notes: This means a בכור that got a blemish. Its meat can't be sold by weight like regular meat, but this kind of weighing is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that step 14 referred to.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בכורות allowing portion-against-portion weighing of a בכור

steps.title: אביי: רבי יהושע may only allow weighing on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's proof. Maybe רבי יהושע allows weighing only on יום טוב, where holy food is not being disrespected. He might forbid it with a בכור, where it is disrespectful to holy food.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Maybe that's not right. רבי יהושע only allowed weighing here, on יום טוב, because no holy food is being disrespected. But there, with a בכור, weighing does disrespect holy food, so maybe he would not allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is attacking רב יוסף's proof. He says the משנה in בכורות might not match רבי יהושע at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed that the same person who allows weighing on יום טוב would also allow it with a בכור. אביי points out that the two cases are different. A בכור is holy food, and weighing it might be disrespectful (בזיון קדשים). So רבי יהושע could allow weighing on יום טוב and still forbid it with a בכור. If so, the משנה in בכורות is not his view.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps it is not so (a way of rejecting a proof)
He only said it in this case and not in others
A firstborn animal, which is holy

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב יוסף, who just brought the proof from בכורות.

phrases.english: But perhaps that is not so;

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָכָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua only said this here,
where there is no disrespect of holy things;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָתָם דְּאִיכָּא בִּזְיוֹן קֳדָשִׁים — לָא.
phrases.english: but there, where there is disrespect of holy things, he did not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from בכורות that was brought in steps 14-15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not reject the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes רבי יהושע would treat a בכור the same as יום טוב. But a בכור also raises the issue of disrespecting holy food.

steps.title: אביי: The רבנן may allow weighing only with a בכור
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a second way to reject the proof. Maybe the רבנן allow weighing with a בכור, since that does not look like weekday business. They might still forbid it on יום טוב, where it does look like weekday business.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or another possibility: the רבנן only allowed weighing there, with a בכור, because it doesn't look like weekday business. But here, on יום טוב, where it does look like weekday business, they would not allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second, different reason why the משנה in בכורות does not prove anything. This time he shows it could even match the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16, אביי argued that רבי יהושע might not agree with the משנה. Now he argues from the other side: the רבנן, who forbid weighing on יום טוב, might agree with the משנה. The problem on יום טוב is that weighing looks like ordinary weekday work. A בכור has no such problem. Either way, the משנה cannot show that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority view that argues with רבי יהושע)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the words "here" and "there." In this step, "there" means the בכור case and "here" means יום טוב, the same as in step 16. What changes is whose opinion is being discussed: now it is the רבנן, not רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: Alternatively,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם
phrases.english: the Rabbis only said it there
phrases.notes: "There" is the בכור, where the משנה allows weighing portion against portion.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא מִחֲזֵי כְּעוֹבָדִין דְּחוֹל,
phrases.english: because it does not look like weekday activity;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דְּמִחֲזֵי כְּעוֹבָדִין דְּחוֹל — לָא.
phrases.english: but here, where it does look like weekday activity, they did not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative way to reject the same proof that step 16 rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from בכורות. It shows the משנה could match the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reason for forbidding weighing on יום טוב (it looks like weekday business) does not apply to a בכור. So the רבנן could agree with that משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי gives two ways the משנה in בכורות could be different from יום טוב. The first is that a בכור involves disrespecting holy food. The second is that only יום טוב has the problem of looking like weekday work. Either way, the משנה is no proof for רבי יהושע.

steps.title: Were רבי חייא and רבי שמעון really that careful with each other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the story in step 11. It asks how רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי could have been strict about equal portions. After all, רבי שמעון did not mind when רבי חייא took five of רבי's seven fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean they were careful with each other about who got what? But there was the story of the seven fish that were brought to רבי's house. Five of them turned up at רבי חייא's house, and רבי שמעון son of רבי did not mind at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story about weighing the meat. Another story shows that these two did not care about exact shares between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only weigh portions against each other if you care that both sides get exactly the same amount. But the fish story shows that רבי חייא and רבי שמעון were so close that רבי שמעון did not mind when רבי חייא took most of the fish. So why would they need to weigh meat?

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (introduces a challenging conclusion)
They were strict with each other (about getting equal shares)
But isn't it so that... (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: Is this to say that they were strict with each other?
phrases.notes: "They" are רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי, who weighed meat in step 11.

phrases.english: But there were those seven fish
that came to Rabbi's house,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִשְׁתַּכַּח חֲמֵשׁ מִנַּיְיהוּ בֵּי רַבִּי חִיָּיא,
phrases.english: and five of them were found at Rabbi Chiya's house,
and Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi did not mind!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the story from step 11 and questions how it could have happened.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story that רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי weighed portions against each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Weighing shows you care about equal shares. But the fish story shows these two did not care about shares at all.

steps.title: רב פפא: Swap one of the names in the story
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that one of the two names must be replaced. The pair who weighed the meat was either רבי חייא with רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, or רבי שמעון ברבי with בר קפרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Put a different person between them. Either it was רבי חייא with רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי, or it was רבי שמעון son of רבי with בר קפרא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question by fixing the names in the story. The two people who weighed the meat were not רבי חייא and רבי שמעון together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem only exists if those two specific people were dividing with each other. Change one of them, and you get a pair who did care about equal shares. That way, the weighing story and the fish story no longer clash. The ruling about weighing on יום טוב stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Throw a person between them (put a different person in the story)

steps.whatToRemember: The story of weighing meat on יום טוב is true. Only the pair of names is changed: either רבי חייא with רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, or רבי שמעון ברבי with בר קפרא.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Throw a person in between them:
phrases.notes: He means: replace one of the two names with someone else.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: either it was Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי וּבַר קַפָּרָא.
phrases.english: or it was Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi and Bar Kappara.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 18 by changing who was in the story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fixing the names of the people in the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The weighing was done between רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי, which clashes with the fish story.
steps.terutzMaskana: The weighing was done by a different pair, who were strict about equal shares.

steps.title: No sharpening a knife on the festival, but running it over another knife is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids sharpening a knife on יום טוב but allows rubbing it against another knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: You may not sharpen a knife on יום טוב, but you may run it over another knife.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: sharpening a knife on יום טוב. The normal way is forbidden, but rubbing one knife against another is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives two cases. Sharpening the regular way is forbidden. Rubbing one knife against another knife is a less usual way, and it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'. It marks the start of the משנה.
Runs it over, rubs it against

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מַשְׁחִיזִין אֶת הַסַּכִּין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not sharpen a knife on a Festival,
but one may run it over another one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מַשְׁחִיזִין אֶת הַסַּכִּין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic, unconnected to the weighing-meat discussion before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Normal sharpening of a knife is forbidden on יום טוב. Rubbing it against another knife is permitted.

steps.title: The ban applies only to a stone sharpener, not a wooden one
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the משנה's ban to a stone sharpener. A wooden sharpener is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב הונא said: The משנה only forbids sharpening with a stone sharpener. With a wooden sharpener, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains how far the משנה's ban reaches. It covers a stone sharpener only, and a wooden sharpener is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stone is the normal tool for sharpening, so using it looks like regular weekday work. A wooden sharpener is not the usual tool, so רב הונא permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this about…' It is a phrase that narrows a rule.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּמַשְׁחֶזֶת שֶׁל אֶבֶן,
phrases.english: They taught this only about a stone sharpener,
but with a wooden sharpener, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּמַשְׁחֶזֶת שֶׁל אֶבֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה's ban to one kind of tool.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sharpening with stone is forbidden. Sharpening with wood is permitted.

steps.title: Stone is forbidden only for sharpening, not for scraping off fat
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says a stone is forbidden only for sharpening. Using it just to remove fat is allowed. So wood must be allowed even for sharpening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: When you said stone is forbidden, that is only to sharpen the knife. To clean off its fat is permitted. From this we learn that with wood, even sharpening is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds a detail to רב הונא's stone case. Stone is forbidden only when you mean to sharpen the blade, not when you just scrape off grease. Then the גמרא draws a conclusion about wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the ban is narrow: only stone, and only for real sharpening. Wood is more lenient than stone, and stone is already allowed for removing fat. So רב הונא's permission for wood must go further than removing fat. The גמרא concludes that wood is allowed even for real sharpening.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That which you said.' It points back to an earlier statement in order to add to it.
To remove its fat or grease
'By implication.' It introduces a conclusion drawn from what was just said.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
That which you said, that stone is forbidden,
we said it only for sharpening it,
but to remove its fat, it is permitted.
This implies that with wood,
even to sharpen it is also permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ שֶׁל אֶבֶן אָסוּר, לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא לְחַדְּדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further limit to the first half of רב הונא's statement (stone).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stone: forbidden only for sharpening, permitted for removing fat. Wood: permitted even for sharpening.

steps.title: Another version: wood is allowed only for scraping off fat
steps.stepSummary: A second version attaches שמואל's comment to the wood case. Wood is allowed only for removing fat, so stone must be forbidden even for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach it on the second half: 'with wood it is permitted.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: When you said wood is permitted, that is only to remove fat. To sharpen is forbidden. From this we learn that with stone, even removing fat is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of שמואל's statement. Here he is commenting on the wood half of רב הונא's words, not the stone half. This version comes out much stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, even wood is allowed only for removing fat. Stone is stricter than wood, so stone must be forbidden even just to remove fat. Real sharpening is forbidden with both tools.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Some teach it…' It introduces another version of where a statement belongs.
The latter half of a statement

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל's words are almost the same in both versions. What changes is which half of רב הונא's statement they are attached to. In step 22, stone is restricted and wood is fully permitted. Here, wood is restricted and stone is fully forbidden.

phrases.english: Some teach it on the latter clause:
'with wood it is permitted.'
phrases.notes: This is the second half of רב הונא's statement in step 21.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
That which you said, that with wood it is permitted,
we said it only for removing its fat,
but to sharpen it is forbidden.
This implies that with stone,
even to remove its fat is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of step 22 by moving שמואל's comment to the wood clause, which leads to a stricter result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood: permitted only for removing fat, forbidden for sharpening. Stone: forbidden even for removing fat.

steps.title: A third version: שמואל comments directly on the משנה
steps.stepSummary: A third version attaches שמואל's comment to the משנה itself. Sharpening is forbidden, removing fat is allowed, and knife-on-knife is allowed even for sharpening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach it on the משנה: 'You may not sharpen a knife on יום טוב.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This is only to sharpen it. To remove its fat is permitted. From this we learn that running it over another knife is permitted even to sharpen it.
steps.whatsHappening: In this third version, שמואל is not commenting on רב הונא at all. He is explaining the משנה's own words, and the גמרא draws a conclusion about the משנה's second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban in the first part of the משנה covers only sharpening, so removing fat the normal way is permitted. That means the permission in the second part, knife over knife, must be about real sharpening. So rubbing knife on knife is allowed even to sharpen.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On our משנה.' It means the statement is attached directly to the משנה.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three versions of שמואל's comment. (1) On stone: stone is forbidden only for sharpening, and wood is allowed even for sharpening. (2) On wood: wood is allowed only for removing fat, and stone is forbidden even for that. (3) On the משנה: normal sharpening is forbidden, removing fat is allowed, and knife-on-knife is allowed even for sharpening.

phrases.english: Some teach it on the Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַשְׁחִיזִין אֶת הַסַּכִּין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: 'One may not sharpen a knife on a Festival.'
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They taught this only about sharpening it,
but to remove its fat is permitted.
This implies that running it over another one
is permitted even to sharpen it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third version of שמואל's statement, attached directly to the משנה instead of to רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's ban covers only sharpening, not removing fat. Knife-on-knife is permitted even for real sharpening.

steps.title: A fourth version: שמואל's comment on the knife-on-knife clause
steps.stepSummary: Some attach שמואל's comment to the end of the משנה. Knife on knife is allowed only to remove fat, not to sharpen. So a sharpener must be forbidden even for removing fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this on the last part of the משנה, 'But one may rub it against another knife.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This was taught only for removing its fat. To sharpen it is forbidden. So we can infer that with a sharpener, even removing its fat is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of where שמואל's comment belongs. Here it goes on the last clause of the משנה, knife against knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even the lenient case, knife on knife, is allowed only for removing fat, then the stricter case, a sharpener, must be forbidden for everything, even just to clean off fat. Like step 24, this version comments on the משנה itself, so it speaks of 'a sharpener' in general. It does not use רב הונא's split between stone and wood.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it (a different version of the statement)
The last part of a משנה
He rubs it (one knife against another)
Its fat (grease stuck on the knife)
By inference, we learn from this that

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the versions. In this version, a sharpener is forbidden even just to remove fat, and knife on knife is allowed only to remove fat, not to sharpen.

phrases.english: And some teach it on the latter clause:
phrases.notes: 'It' means שמואל's comment from the earlier versions.

phrases.english: But one may run it over another (knife).
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They taught this only to remove its fat,
but to sharpen it, it is forbidden.
This shows by inference that with a sharpener,
even to remove its fat is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth version of שמואל's comment, placed on the last clause of the משנה instead of on the stone, the wood, or the משנה as a whole.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Knife on knife is allowed only to remove fat. A sharpener is forbidden even for removing fat.

steps.title: Who forbids using a sharpener?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that using a sharpener is forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that with a sharpener it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה's ban on a sharpener follows. This sets up the next step, where רב חסדא answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sharpening a knife is not cooking itself. It only prepares a tool for cooking. The גמרא wants to know which תנא forbids that kind of preparation on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא? (Whose opinion is this?)
A sharpener (a stone used to sharpen knives)

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who holds that with a sharpener it is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the details of the versions to the basic question of whose view the משנה follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא forbids sharpening a knife on a sharpener on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב חסדא: Not like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה does not follow רבי יהודה. A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה permits מכשירי אוכל נפש on יום טוב, while the תנא קמא permits only the food preparation itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is not like רבי יהודה. As a ברייתא teaches: The only difference between יום טוב and שבת is food preparation. רבי יהודה permits even things that make food preparation possible.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. The ban on a sharpener follows the תנא קמא, not רבי יהודה, and he brings a ברייתא to show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows on יום טוב only work done directly on food. רבי יהודה also allows preparing the tools needed for food, like sharpening a knife. So the משנה, which forbids the sharpener, cannot follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Food preparation (work done directly on food)
Things that make food preparation possible, like fixing tools

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's ban on a sharpener follows the תנא קמא. רבי יהודה would allow it because he permits מכשירי אוכל נפש.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.
As it is taught in a baraita:
There is no difference between a Festival and Shabbat
except for food preparation alone.
Rabbi Yehuda permits
even things that make food preparation possible.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban follows the תנא קמא of the ברייתא. רבי יהודה permits מכשירי אוכל נפש and would allow sharpening.

steps.title: רבא: We quote you as ruling like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב חסדא that people teach in his name that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. רב חסדא happily agrees and wishes that all such good teachings be said in his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב חסדא: We teach in your name that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. He answered him: May it be God's will that you teach all fine teachings like this in my name.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reports a ruling quoted in רב חסדא's name: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. רב חסדא accepts it with a blessing, which shows he agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 only said whose view the משנה follows. It did not say what the final הלכה is. Here we learn the practical ruling: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, so מכשירי אוכל נפש are allowed on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: We teach publicly in your name

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical ruling. Even though our משנה forbids the sharpener, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who allows preparing food tools on יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not upset that people quote him. His blessing means he is glad, and he agrees that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Chisda:
We teach in your name
that the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda.
He said to him: May it be (God's) will
that all fine teachings like these
you should teach in my name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא: דָּרְשִׁינַן מִשְּׁמָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After identifying the opinions, this gives the practical הלכה in favor of רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: מכשירי אוכל נפש are permitted on יום טוב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חסדא agrees that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רב נחמיה begins a story about רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמיה בריה דרב יוסף starts telling what he saw while standing before רבא. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמיה son of רב יוסף said: I was standing before רבא, and he was...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story about what רבא did. This only sets up the story, and the main part comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story will show רבא's practice, most likely about this same topic of preparing a knife on יום טוב. For now, we only hear who is telling the story and that he was standing in front of רבא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Nechemya, son of Rav Yosef, said:
I was standing before Rava,
and he was...
phrases.notes: The sentence stops here. It finishes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a story about רבא, right after the ruling in favor of רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of a story. No ruling has been given yet.
